Interpretation and proof ceiling

Whoami demand fell approximately 4.3-4.4x. Per-call seat_list/role/fyi/active times are lower, but lower host load, different request/seat mix and pool contention can affect them. Do not normalize all daemon/thread CPU by whoami calls and call that a pool saving: the daemon also runs background, observer and other request work. The observed whole-daemon and SQLite/Tokio CPU decreases are not exclusively attributable to #321; the measurements also cannot establish that a particular fraction belongs to #318 or the changed cohort.

The final performance verdict remains the verified source model: two warm clean one-query pooled leases take 10 -> 4 SQLite-worker dispatch/reply operations, 6 -> 2 directly initiated on the request path. This is not every store-call or transaction shape. The logged historical schema-only benchmark covers one lease (5 -> 2 total worker commands), not the two-lease headline; the earlier verdict verified its retained output, not a presently retained rerunnable benchmark implementation. This AFTER note does not upgrade that proof grade or request moving the schema brake.

No new loop, poll, timer or process-launch site is introduced by the pool hook change. Its savings scale per reused clean lease at whatever request/background rate the fleet actually generates; dirty cleanup retains its flush/rollback costs. No destructive operation or retention policy was added.
